source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Ectopic pregnancy, because pain and vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy can signal implantation outside the uterus and possible rupture.","B":"Normal implantation discomfort, because unilateral pain with bleeding is expected and does not require assessment for a pregnancy complication.","C":"Uncomplicated cystitis, because urinary infection is the primary explanation for unilateral pelvic pain with vaginal bleeding in pregnancy.","D":"Routine gastroenteritis, because gastrointestinal infection best explains vaginal bleeding in a client with a positive pregnancy test."}}
source_row.rationale: A positive pregnancy test with unilateral pelvic or abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding warrants prompt evaluation for ectopic pregnancy because rupture can cause life-threatening hemorrhage.
source_row.source_detail: Symptoms and diagnosis sections: abnormal vaginal bleeding and pelvic/abdominal pain are ectopic pregnancy warning symptoms; rupture can cause life-threatening internal bleeding. source_row.stem: A client with a positive pregnancy test has unilateral lower abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. Which condition must be evaluated promptly?
